344|
345|Factories
346|~~~~~~~~~
347|
348|Use factories to harness Arrow's module API for a custom Arrow-derived type.  First, derive your type:
349|
350|.. code-block:: python
351|
352|    >>> class CustomArrow(arrow.Arrow):
353|    ...
354|    ...     def days_till_xmas(self):
355|    ...
356|    ...         xmas = arrow.Arrow(self.year, 12, 25)
357|    ...
358|    ...         if self > xmas:
359|    ...             xmas = xmas.shift(years=1)
360|    ...
361|    ...         return (xmas - self).days
362|
363|
364|Then get and use a factory for it:
365|
366|.. code-block:: python
367|
368|    >>> factory = arrow.ArrowFactory(CustomArrow)
369|    >>> custom = factory.utcnow()
370|    >>> custom
371|    >>> <CustomArrow [2013-05-27T23:35:35.533160+00:00]>
372|
373|    >>> custom.days_till_xmas()
374|    >>> 211
375|
376|.. _supported-tokens:
377|
378|Supported Tokens
379|~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
380|
381|Use the following tokens for parsing and formatting. Note that they are **not** the same as the tokens for `strptime <https://linux.die.net/man/3/strptime>`_:
382|
383|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
384||                                |Token         |Output                                     |
385|+================================+==============+===========================================+
386||**Year**                        |YYYY          |2000, 2001, 2002 ... 2012, 2013            |
387|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
388||                                |YY            |00, 01, 02 ... 12, 13                      |
389|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
390||**Month**                       |MMMM          |January, February, March ... [#t1]_        |
391|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
392||                                |MMM           |Jan, Feb, Mar ... [#t1]_                   |
393|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
394||                                |MM            |01, 02, 03 ... 11, 12                      |
395|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
396||                                |M             |1, 2, 3 ... 11, 12                         |
397|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
398||**Day of Year**                 |DDDD          |001, 002, 003 ... 364, 365                 |
399|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
400||                                |DDD           |1, 2, 3 ... 364, 365                       |
401|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
402||**Day of Month**                |DD            |01, 02, 03 ... 30, 31                      |
403|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
404||                                |D             |1, 2, 3 ... 30, 31                         |
405|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
406||                                |Do            |1st, 2nd, 3rd ... 30th, 31st               |
407|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
408||**Day of Week**                 |dddd          |Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday ... [#t2]_      |
409|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
410||                                |ddd           |Mon, Tue, Wed ... [#t2]_                   |
411|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
412||                                |d             |1, 2, 3 ... 6, 7                           |
413|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
414||**ISO week date**               |W             |2011-W05-4, 2019-W17                       |
415|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
416||**Hour**                        |HH            |00, 01, 02 ... 23, 24                      |
417|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
418||                                |H             |0, 1, 2 ... 23, 24                         |
419|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
420||                                |hh            |01, 02, 03 ... 11, 12                      |
421|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
422||                                |h             |1, 2, 3 ... 11, 12                         |
423|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
424||**AM / PM**                     |A             |AM, PM, am, pm [#t1]_                      |
425|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
426||                                |a             |am, pm [#t1]_                              |
427|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
428||**Minute**                      |mm            |00, 01, 02 ... 58, 59                      |
429|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
430||                                |m             |0, 1, 2 ... 58, 59                         |
431|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
432||**Second**                      |ss            |00, 01, 02 ... 58, 59                      |
433|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
434||                                |s             |0, 1, 2 ... 58, 59                         |
435|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
436||**Sub-second**                  |S...          |0, 02, 003, 000006, 123123123123... [#t3]_ |
437|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
438||**Timezone**                    |ZZZ           |Asia/Baku, Europe/Warsaw, GMT ... [#t4]_   |
439|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
440||                                |ZZ            |-07:00, -06:00 ... +06:00, +07:00, +08, Z  |
441|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
442||                                |Z             |-0700, -0600 ... +0600, +0700, +08, Z      |
443|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
444||**Seconds Timestamp**           |X             |1381685817, 1381685817.915482 ... [#t5]_   |
445|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
446||**ms or µs Timestamp**          |x             |1569980330813, 1569980330813221            |
447|+--------------------------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------+
448|
449|.. rubric:: Footnotes
450|
451|.. [#t1] localization support for parsing and formatting
452|.. [#t2] localization support only for formatting
453|.. [#t3] the result is truncated to microseconds, with `half-to-even rounding <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_floating_point#Roundings_to_nearest>`_.
454|.. [#t4] timezone names from `tz database <https://www.iana.org/time-zones>`_ provided via dateutil package, note that abbreviations such as MST, PDT, BRST are unlikely to parse due to ambiguity. Use the full IANA zone name instead (Asia/Shanghai, Europe/London, America/Chicago etc).
455|.. [#t5] this token cannot be used for parsing timestamps out of natural language strings due to compatibility reasons
456|
457|Built-in Formats
458|++++++++++++++++
459|
460|There are several formatting standards that are provided as built-in tokens.
461|
462|.. code-block:: python
463|
464|    >>> arw = arrow.utcnow()
465|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_ATOM)
466|    '2020-05-27 10:30:35+00:00'
467|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_COOKIE)
468|    'Wednesday, 27-May-2020 10:30:35 UTC'
469|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RSS)
470|    'Wed, 27 May 2020 10:30:35 +0000'
471|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC822)
472|    'Wed, 27 May 20 10:30:35 +0000'
473|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC850)
474|    'Wednesday, 27-May-20 10:30:35 UTC'
475|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC1036)
476|    'Wed, 27 May 20 10:30:35 +0000'
477|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC1123)
478|    'Wed, 27 May 2020 10:30:35 +0000'
479|    >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC2822)
480|    'Wed, 27 May 2020 10:30:35 +0000'
481|     >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC3339)
482|    '2020-05-27 10:30:35+00:00'
483|     >>> arw.format(arrow.FORMAT_W3C)
484|    '2020-05-27 10:30:35+00:00'
485|
486|Escaping Formats
487|~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
488|
489|Tokens, phrases, and regular expressions in a format string can be escaped when parsing and formatting by enclosing them within square brackets.
490|
491|Tokens & Phrases
492|++++++++++++++++
493|
494|Any `token <Supported Tokens_>`_ or phrase can be escaped as follows:
495|
496|.. code-block:: python
497|
498|    >>> fmt = "YYYY-MM-DD h [h] m"
499|    >>> arw = arrow.get("2018-03-09 8 h 40", fmt)
500|    <Arrow [2018-03-09T08:40:00+00:00]>
501|    >>> arw.format(fmt)
502|    '2018-03-09 8 h 40'
503|
504|    >>> fmt = "YYYY-MM-DD h [hello] m"
505|    >>> arw = arrow.get("2018-03-09 8 hello 40", fmt)
506|    <Arrow [2018-03-09T08:40:00+00:00]>
507|    >>> arw.format(fmt)
508|    '2018-03-09 8 hello 40'
509|
510|    >>> fmt = "YYYY-MM-DD h [hello world] m"
511|    >>> arw = arrow.get("2018-03-09 8 hello world 40", fmt)
512|    <Arrow [2018-03-09T08:40:00+00:00]>
513|    >>> arw.format(fmt)
514|    '2018-03-09 8 hello world 40'
515|
516|This can be useful for parsing dates in different locales such as French, in which it is common to format time strings as "8 h 40" rather than "8:40".
517|
518|Regular Expressions
519|+++++++++++++++++++
520|
521|You can also escape regular expressions by enclosing them within square brackets. In the following example, we are using the regular expression :code:`\s+` to match any number of whitespace characters that separate the tokens. This is useful if you do not know the number of spaces between tokens ahead of time (e.g. in log files).
522|
523|.. code-block:: python
524|
525|    >>> fmt = r"ddd[\s+]MMM[\s+]DD[\s+]HH:mm:ss[\s+]YYYY"
526|    >>> arrow.get("Mon Sep 08 16:41:45 2014", fmt)
527|    <Arrow [2014-09-08T16:41:45+00:00]>
528|
529|    >>> arrow.get("Mon \tSep 08   16:41:45     2014", fmt)
530|    <Arrow [2014-09-08T16:41:45+00:00]>
531|
532|    >>> arrow.get("Mon Sep 08   16:41:45   2014", fmt)
533|    <Arrow [2014-09-08T16:41:45+00:00]>
534|
535|Punctuation
536|~~~~~~~~~~~
537|
538|Date and time formats may be fenced on either side by one punctuation character from the following list: ``, . ; : ? ! " \` ' [ ] { } ( ) < >``
539|
540|.. code-block:: python
541|
542|    >>> arrow.get("Cool date: 2019-10-31T09:12:45.123456+04:30.", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SZZ")
543|    <Arrow [2019-10-31T09:12:45.123456+04:30]>
544|
545|    >>> arrow.get("Tomorrow (2019-10-31) is Halloween!", "YYYY-MM-DD")
546|    <Arrow [2019-10-31T00:00:00+00:00]>
547|
548|    >>> arrow.get("Halloween is on 2019.10.31.", "YYYY.MM.DD")
549|    <Arrow [2019-10-31T00:00:00+00:00]>
550|
551|    >>> arrow.get("It's Halloween tomorrow (2019-10-31)!", "YYYY-MM-DD")
552|    # Raises exception because there are multiple punctuation marks following the date
553|
554|Redundant Whitespace
555|~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
556|
557|Redundant whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, and newlines) can be normalized automatically by passing in the ``normalize_whitespace`` flag to ``arrow.get``:
558|
559|.. code-block:: python
560|
561|    >>> arrow.get('\t \n  2013-05-05T12:30:45.123456 \t \n', normalize_whitespace=True)
562|    <Arrow [2013-05-05T12:30:45.123456+00:00]>
563|
564|    >>> arrow.get('2013-05-05  T \n   12:30:45\t123456', 'YYYY-MM-DD T HH:mm:ss S', normalize_whitespace=True)
565|    <Arrow [2013-05-05T12:30:45.123456+00:00]>

30|
31|**Arrow** is a Python library that offers a sensible and human-friendly approach to creating, manipulating, formatting and converting dates, times and timestamps. It implements and updates the datetime type, plugging gaps in functionality and providing an intelligent module API that supports many common creation scenarios. Simply put, it helps you work with dates and times with fewer imports and a lot less code.
32|
33|Arrow is named after the `arrow of time <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_of_time>`_ and is heavily inspired by `moment.js <https://github.com/moment/moment>`_ and `requests <https://github.com/psf/requests>`_.
34|
35|Why use Arrow over built-in modules?
36|------------------------------------
37|
38|Python's standard library and some other low-level modules have near-complete date, time and timezone functionality, but don't work very well from a usability perspective:
39|
40|- Too many modules: datetime, time, calendar, dateutil, pytz and more
41|- Too many types: date, time, datetime, tzinfo, timedelta, relativedelta, etc.
42|- Timezones and timestamp conversions are verbose and unpleasant
43|- Timezone naivety is the norm
44|- Gaps in functionality: ISO 8601 parsing, timespans, humanization
45|
46|Features
47|--------
48|
49|- Fully-implemented, drop-in replacement for datetime
50|- Support for Python 3.8+
51|- Timezone-aware and UTC by default
52|- Super-simple creation options for many common input scenarios
53|- ``shift`` method with support for relative offsets, including weeks
54|- Format and parse strings automatically
55|- Wide support for the `ISO 8601 <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601>`_ standard
56|- Timezone conversion
57|- Support for ``dateutil``, ``pytz``, and ``ZoneInfo`` tzinfo objects
58|- Generates time spans, ranges, floors and ceilings for time frames ranging from microsecond to year
59|- Humanize dates and times with a growing list of contributed locales
60|- Extensible for your own Arrow-derived types
61|- Full support for PEP 484-style type hints
62|
63|Quick Start
64|-----------
65|
66|Installation
67|~~~~~~~~~~~~
68|
69|To install Arrow, use `pip <https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/quickstart/>`_ or `pipenv <https://docs.pipenv.org>`_:
70|
71|.. code-block:: console
72|
73|    $ pip install -U arrow
74|
75|Example Usage
76|~~~~~~~~~~~~~
77|
78|.. code-block:: python
79|
80|    >>> import arrow
81|    >>> arrow.get('2013-05-11T21:23:58.970460+07:00')
82|    <Arrow [2013-05-11T21:23:58.970460+07:00]>
83|
84|    >>> utc = arrow.utcnow()
85|    >>> utc
86|    <Arrow [2013-05-11T21:23:58.970460+00:00]>
87|
88|    >>> utc = utc.shift(hours=-1)
89|    >>> utc
90|    <Arrow [2013-05-11T20:23:58.970460+00:00]>
91|
92|    >>> local = utc.to('US/Pacific')
93|    >>> local
94|    <Arrow [2013-05-11T13:23:58.970460-07:00]>
95|
96|    >>> local.timestamp()
97|    1368303838.970460
98|
99|    >>> local.format()
100|    '2013-05-11 13:23:58 -07:00'
101|
102|    >>> local.format('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss ZZ')
103|    '2013-05-11 13:23:58 -07:00'
104|
105|    >>> local.humanize()
106|    'an hour ago'
107|
108|    >>> local.humanize(locale='ko-kr')
109|    '한시간 전'
110|

114|-------------
115|
116|For full documentation, please visit `arrow.readthedocs.io <https://arrow.readthedocs.io>`_.
117|
118|Contributing
119|------------
120|
121|Contributions are welcome for both code and localizations (adding and updating locales). Begin by gaining familiarity with the Arrow library and its features. Then, jump into contributing:
122|
123|#. Find an issue or feature to tackle on the `issue tracker <https://github.com/arrow-py/arrow/issues>`_. Issues marked with the `"good first issue" label <https://github.com/arrow-py/arrow/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22>`_ may be a great place to start!
124|#. Fork `this repository <https://github.com/arrow-py/arrow>`_ on GitHub and begin making changes in a branch.
125|#. Add a few tests to ensure that the bug was fixed or the feature works as expected.
126|#. Run the entire test suite and linting checks by running one of the following commands: ``tox && tox -e lint,docs`` (if you have `tox <https://tox.readthedocs.io>`_ installed) **OR** ``make build39 && make test && make lint`` (if you do not have Python 3.9 installed, replace ``build39`` with the latest Python version on your system).
127|#. Submit a pull request and await feedback 😃.
128|
129|If you have any questions along the way, feel free to ask them `here <https://github.com/arrow-py/arrow/discussions>`_.
130|

521|class TestArrowFalsePositiveDst:
522|    """These tests relate to issues #376 and #551.
523|    The key points in both issues are that arrow will assign a UTC timezone if none is provided and
524|    .to() will change other attributes to be correct whereas .replace() only changes the specified attribute.
525|
526|    Issue 376
527|    >>> arrow.get('2016-11-06').to('America/New_York').ceil('day')
528|    < Arrow [2016-11-05T23:59:59.999999-04:00] >
529|
530|    Issue 551
531|    >>> just_before = arrow.get('2018-11-04T01:59:59.999999')
532|    >>> just_before
533|    2018-11-04T01:59:59.999999+00:00
534|    >>> just_after = just_before.shift(microseconds=1)
535|    >>> just_after
536|    2018-11-04T02:00:00+00:00
537|    >>> just_before_eastern = just_before.replace(tzinfo='US/Eastern')
538|    >>> just_before_eastern
539|    2018-11-04T01:59:59.999999-04:00
540|    >>> just_after_eastern = just_after.replace(tzinfo='US/Eastern')
541|    >>> just_after_eastern
542|    2018-11-04T02:00:00-05:00
543|    """
544|
545|    def test_dst(self):
546|        self.before_1 = arrow.Arrow(
547|            2016, 11, 6, 3, 59, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
548|        )
549|        self.before_2 = arrow.Arrow(2016, 11, 6, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York"))
550|        self.after_1 = arrow.Arrow(2016, 11, 6, 4, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York"))
551|        self.after_2 = arrow.Arrow(
552|            2016, 11, 6, 23, 59, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
553|        )
554|        self.before_3 = arrow.Arrow(
555|            2018, 11, 4, 3, 59, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
556|        )
557|        self.before_4 = arrow.Arrow(2018, 11, 4, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York"))
558|        self.after_3 = arrow.Arrow(2018, 11, 4, 4, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York"))
559|        self.after_4 = arrow.Arrow(
560|            2018, 11, 4, 23, 59, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
561|        )
562|        assert self.before_1.day == self.before_2.day
563|        assert self.after_1.day == self.after_2.day
564|        assert self.before_3.day == self.before_4.day
565|        assert self.after_3.day == self.after_4.day

169|
170|After 8 years we're pleased to announce Arrow v1.0. Thanks to the entire Python community for helping make Arrow the amazing package it is today!
171|
172|- [CHANGE] Arrow has **dropped support** for Python 2.7 and 3.5.
173|- [CHANGE] There are multiple **breaking changes** with this release, please see the `migration guide <https://github.com/arrow-py/arrow/issues/832>`_ for a complete overview.
174|- [CHANGE] Arrow is now following `semantic versioning <https://semver.org/>`_.
175|- [CHANGE] Made ``humanize`` granularity="auto" limits more accurate to reduce strange results.
176|- [NEW] Added support for Python 3.9.
177|- [NEW] Added a new keyword argument "exact" to ``span``, ``span_range`` and ``interval`` methods. This makes timespans begin at the start time given and not extend beyond the end time given, for example:
178|
179|.. code-block:: python
180|
181|    >>> start = Arrow(2021, 2, 5, 12, 30)
182|    >>> end = Arrow(2021, 2, 5, 17, 15)
183|    >>> for r in arrow.Arrow.span_range('hour', start, end, exact=True):
184|    ...     print(r)
185|    ...
186|    (<Arrow [2021-02-05T12:30:00+00:00]>, <Arrow [2021-02-05T13:29:59.999999+00:00]>)
187|    (<Arrow [2021-02-05T13:30:00+00:00]>, <Arrow [2021-02-05T14:29:59.999999+00:00]>)
188|    (<Arrow [2021-02-05T14:30:00+00:00]>, <Arrow [2021-02-05T15:29:59.999999+00:00]>)
189|    (<Arrow [2021-02-05T15:30:00+00:00]>, <Arrow [2021-02-05T16:29:59.999999+00:00]>)
190|    (<Arrow [2021-02-05T16:30:00+00:00]>, <Arrow [2021-02-05T17:14:59.999999+00:00]>)
191|
192|- [NEW] Arrow now natively supports PEP 484-style type annotations.
193|- [FIX] Fixed handling of maximum permitted timestamp on Windows systems.
194|- [FIX] Corrections to French, German, Japanese and Norwegian locales.
